Row selection is done by slicing x.data and reconstructing an STSList (carrying alphabet, markers, weights and ids, with issues remapped by sequences._remap_issues), or for a quick view by copying and reassigning .data. Both routes are exercised end-to-end into seqdist by the cited test. Earlier wording claiming 'STSList indexing' described a capability that was never implemented.

Palette retrieval preserves the STSList state order, returns the configured colors without mutating metadata, and returns an independent Python list. Length diverges: R's cpal returns one color per real state, traminex one per codebook entry. Marker padding: STSList uses one integer codebook in which x.alphabet includes declared nr and void markers at their actual code positions, so this per-state result carries len(x.alphabet) entries where R returns statl (+ nr when missing is included). Real-state values agree exactly; marker entries contain configured colors (default missing darkgrey and void white), even when unused. The padding is NOT uniform across the package - seqstatf and seqtrate follow the real alphabet exactly as R does - so it is a per-function decision, pinned by tests/test_per_state_shape_and_selection.py. Declared external markers are read through the canonical codebook, so both marker representations return the same padded result.
Python direct STSList.cpal mutation replaces R cpal<-; valid palettes are visible through cpal, but post-construction assignment does not run the R length check.

All weight-permutation methods have exact deterministic sufficient statistics and seeded local reproducibility; NumPy's local RNG stream intentionally differs from R's global RNG stream for sampled permutations. 2026-10-22 (TX-AUD-20261019-046): groups are R's factor() levels, each named as R's as.character writes it (1, 9.5, 1e+05; it read 1.0) and numbers equal to 15 significant digits one group (0.3 and 0.1 + 0.2), R-golden tested. A group whose weights sum to a negative total is computed and only an exact 0 total gives discrepancy 0 (dissassocweighted.R:313-330); the Levene residuals use R's weighted.mean, sum((x*w)[w != 0]) / sum(w), unguarded (TX-AUD-20261010-079; R golden make_goldens_diss_trees_reps.R). Group and total inertias are summed in tmrWeightedInertiaDist's order (weighted_inertia), vectorised; the permutation test on 712 weighted cases with R = 200 is about 1.8 times faster than with the per-row loop and still several times slower than R (TX-AUD-20261010-083). A whole number beyond R's integer range (+-2147483647) is a double, as R holds it, so two 64-bit integers equal as doubles form one group named as R writes the double (batch-12 review M-5; R golden g_int64). A zero total weight gives R's floating-point results (the total discrepancy and the statistics NaN), where Python's float division raised ZeroDivisionError (TX-AUD-20261010-096; R golden make_goldens_statistics_items.R).

Weighted and unweighted group centers, all-center distances, squared distances, and medoids-first ordering match TraMineR. Deliberate divergence: medoids.index=TRUE errors in R (TRUE is mapped to 'First' and then rejected); traminex accepts True as 'first'. Extension: R stops when group has a missing value (every mode); traminex leaves such a case out of every group (0 in the default mode, its distance to each centre with allcenter, never a medoid). 2026-10-22 (TX-AUD-20261019-046): groups are R's factor() levels, named as R names them (allcenter columns 1, 1e+05; they read 1.0) and numbers equal to 15 significant digits one group, R-golden tested; the medoid dict stays keyed by group value (a merged level by its first value). Contributions are summed in tmrWeightedInertiaContrib's order (cases in index order), so identical cases tie exactly and the first is the medoid, as in R (TX-AUD-20261011-023). The weighted mean subtracted from the contributions is R's weighted.mean, sum((x*w)[w != 0]) / sum(w) with R's long-double sum(), so the values equal R's to the last bit (batch-12 review M-4; R golden make_goldens_diss_trees_reps.R disscenter_64_3).

Weighted Spearman midranks ties correlations p-values and every documented what route match TraMineR 2.2-14. A reported Spearman difference from R (TX-AUD-20261011-066) was not reproduced: on the same input R and traminex agree to about 1e-15; the report had compared traminex on matrices read back from 15-digit text with R in memory.

Small-group merging preserves TraMineR membership updates, weighted inertia comparisons, and deterministic group ordering. Cycle-7 W-07: silent defaults to True here where dissmergegroups.R:77 defaults it to FALSE -- a printed-progress difference only, with the returned group and quality identical either way; it is the single default divergence found by the golden default-coverage sweep. Corrected R defect (2026-10-17, TX-AUD-20261011-016): when no merge leaves a positive quality (no pair loses less than the reference quality) and the reference quality is 0 or below (or crit = 1: the stop test diff > crit * quality.ref, dissmergegroups.R:165), R's loop takes the merge branch with nothing to merge, prints 'Merging groups and' and does not end (dissmergegroups.R:127-168); traminex stops and returns the grouping unchanged (R-golden tested: R does not finish within 5 s; a merging control, and a negative reference quality with a merge of positive quality, give R's result, 2026-10-18). 2026-10-22 (TX-AUD-20261019-046): groups are numbered as R's as.integer(factor(group)) (dissmergegroups.R:105), so numbers equal to 15 significant digits are one group (0.3 and 0.1 + 0.2), R-golden tested.

Formula-order weighted and unweighted deterministic decompositions are R-golden exact; permutation p-values use an isolated NumPy PCG64 stream rather than R global Mersenne-Twister draws. Terms are a mapping of named predictors: there is no formula interface and no interaction term (give a product column instead). Corrected R defect (2026-10-17, TX-AUD-20261010-040): on a rank-deficient design R builds its hat matrices from all ncol(X) columns of qr.Q(qr(X)) and counts degrees of freedom in columns (dissmfacw.R:67-69), so the projection gains one arbitrary direction; traminex projects onto the column space (pivoted QR, R's tolerance 1e-7) and counts ranks, so the model and every estimable term have the values of the same design without its redundant columns (R-golden tested against R on that design), and a term that adds no rank given the others has NaN statistics, with a warning. 2026-10-22 (TX-REP-20261019-002): the rank and the kept columns are R's qr() rule, LINPACK dqrdc2 with tol 1e-7 on the weighted design (dissmfacw.R:67): a column is set aside when its remaining norm falls below 1e-7 of its own norm. The rule above (pivots above 1e-7 of the largest) dropped columns of designs whose columns differ greatly in scale (a column scaled by 1e9: rank 1 where R has 3). R-golden tested on such a design, weighted and unweighted.

Deterministic density, frequency, and distance criteria plus quality statistics remain R-golden exact; criterion=random uses NumPy global draws rather than R global draws, so sampled representatives can differ. On an exact tie between scores (equal in exact arithmetic) R's choice depends on its BLAS's summation order: on mvad (LCS, weighted) rows 59 and 334 (1-based) tie, R's OpenBLAS ranks 334 first and keeps it as the fourth representative; traminex sums such scores with correct rounding and keeps the lower row first, as R's order() does on a tie (tests/test_dissrep_exact_ties.py; TX-AUD-20261019-017). Weights without a positive total are refused with a ValueError naming them; R stops too, on the NaN of a division by that total (missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed; 2026-10-25 study finding F-05, fixed 2026-11-07; R golden make_goldens_study_findings.R).

All prop first and random grouping contracts are covered including squared and pow dispersion and wcmdscale-equivalent weighted default MDS; random_state uses an isolated NumPy generator instead of R's global RNG while preserving deterministic ordering and group invariants. Medoids are R's exact first minimum (TX-AUD-20261011-023): the inertia contributions are summed in tmrWeightedInertiaContrib's order, so identical cases tie exactly as in R; the former near-tie tolerance (np.isclose, rtol and atol 1e-12), which chose endpoint 0 of the [0,s,2s] control at scales 1e-14 and 1e-20 where R chooses the middle case, is removed (R golden make_goldens_diss_trees_reps.R). Corrected R ambiguity (2026-10-18, TX-REP-20261017-006): the default one-dimensional MDS axis (sortv = 'mds') has no sign of its own; R takes it from LAPACK, so its groups, medoids and R2 follow the numerical library (on one input R with OpenBLAS 0.3.26 gives the negation of SciPy's LAPACK 3.9.0). traminex orients the axis so that the coordinate of largest absolute value is positive (coordinates within a relative 1e-10 of that value are tied and the first decides, so symmetric data, whose tied coordinates differ only in rounding, give the same groups on every build; zero-weight NA coordinates ignored); R-golden tested against R's seqrf given the axis oriented by that rule. The default MDS axis does not depend on the scale of the distances: the repeated-leading-root test (traminex's index-order fallback; R's cmdscale has none) is relative, rtol 1e-12, where an absolute 1e-12 sent distances near 1e-10 to index order (TX-AUD-20261011-052; R golden make_goldens_diss_trees_reps.R). A text or categorical sortv is ordered as R's order(sortv) (dissrf.R:94): text in R's collation, a categorical by its codes, missing values last, through the order keys shared with sequence_index_plot (TX-REP-20261021-001; R golden make_goldens_diss_trees_reps.R).

R=1 tree structure and weighted split statistics remain R-golden exact; R>1 split and final-adjustment permutation decisions use an isolated NumPy stream and can change the returned tree. With weights, weight_permutation 'permute' and 'random-sampling' are refused: R runs them, but its split test then replicates cases by weights truncated to integers (disstree.dissassoc.R:52-64). 2026-10-22 (TX-AUD-20261011-055): a predictor's levels are R's factor() levels (disstree.R:404): numbers equal to 15 significant digits are one level (0.3 and 0.1 + 0.2 no longer split), and a numeric split's break is the level text read back as a number (disstree.R:544: a predictor at 1/3 splits at 0.333333333333333). R-golden tested. Node medoids break ties between identical cases as R does: contributions in tmrWeightedInertiaContrib's order (TX-AUD-20261011-023; R golden make_goldens_diss_trees_reps.R, the weighted mvad tree). random_state defaults to None, fresh randomness for the permutation tests: R's function has no seed argument and draws from R's global stream, so neither reproduces the other's permutations; pass random_state for reproducible results (TX-AUD-20261011-066).

Case-to-leaf assignments are 1-based rule indexes, matching R and the golden terminal partition, without mutating the tree. These differ from the tree node IDs returned by disstreeleaf. Covariate names with dots and R backquoted names are read as R reads them. Divergence (R defect): for a non-syntactic covariate name such as my var, R's disstree.get.rules writes the bare name (my var <= 5) and records it backquoted, so R's disstree.assign stops with 'covariates missing in profile' or a parse error; Python assigns those rules to the leaf each case's covariates satisfy. A None rule (R's NA rule of a root-only tree) matches no profile, so the result is NaN, as R's NA; R's rules carry their covariates as an attribute, which a Python list cannot, so that rule names no covariate to check (TX-AUD-20261019-047). Rule levels are read as R's parser reads them (TX-AUD-20261010-065): ' & ' inside a quoted level belongs to the level; single or double quotes and backslash escapes are read; text R cannot parse (a doubled quote, or R's own rule for a level holding a quote) raises ValueError, as R stops. Escapes in a level follow R's string table (\n, \t and the other single-character escapes, octal, \x, \u, \U); an escape R does not know, a missing hex digit or a nul raises ValueError, as R stops (batch-12 review M-3; R golden rule_escape_1 to _24).

The weighted value adds w[j] * w[i] * D[j, i] and the weight total in tmrWeightedInertiaDist's order, equal to R's to the last bit (TX-AUD-20261010-083; R golden make_goldens_diss_trees_reps.R).

Promoted R internal, and a name collision rather than a port. R's TraMineR:::entropy(distrib, base) is the Shannon entropy of a probability vector (entropy(c(.5,.5)) = 0.693147180559945). traminex's entropy(x: STSList, normalized=True) is the global Shannon entropy over all state cells of a sequence object (the void padding of unequal lengths is not a state), optionally divided by log(K). The two take different inputs and answer different questions; neither reimplements the other. A zero frequency contributes 0, as R's entropy.R:5-7 drops it, so uniform data give exactly 1 normalized (it added 1e-12 inside the log: 0.9999999999971146); the missing state is one of the K states when the codebook has the missing marker (TX-AUD-20261010-095).

Squared and unsquared weighted double-centering, including the default, reproduce TraMineR gower_matrix values and symmetry; a weight total of zero gives R's NaN and a negative total R's finite values (s = weights/sum(weights), dissmfacw.R:20), where traminex refused both (TX-AUD-20261011-005).
